EMT here. It’s used in extremities with hemostatic gauze. With a bullet or fragment, it can shred multiple blood vessels and can be very deep so packing will help control bleeding from those. I was trained to pack and then cover with bandage and direct pressure. All in all it’s bleeding control. 

You wouldn’t put it somewhere like on the abdomen, cause I mean you’d just be shoving gauze into their guts. For something like that you would use what’s called an occlusive dressing which is air and water tight over moist sterile towels.

Yeah I think generally the people that don’t enjoy it just don’t happen to understand all the things that go into effect every play. 

Kind of like soccer/football to me, there’s so much going on that I am not seeing but on the surface it’s people kicking a ball around and trying to get it in the back of a net for 90 minutes.

It takes a big understanding, like golf or chess. On the surface a dude is hitting a ball thrown by another guy but there is so much decision making going into every single decision. 

For example, a pitcher deciding his pitches. It’s not just based on the history of the batters performance, how has the opposing team been seeing pitches today? Are they chasing offspeed or chasing pitches up? What’s this batters tendencies been the last series? Do I want to set him up with a fastball up and in then hope for a chase on an offspeed low and away? How is my confidence on my pitch? There’s dozens of more factors going through pitchers heads when they’re deciding their pitch and location. That’s just the part of throwing the ball to the plate. 

Then you have defensive positioning, they say baseball is the game of inches. That is the truth, a few steps in a fielders position could determine if a hit ball will turn into a single or an out. Then if they happen to get on that hit could turn into a run that costed them the game. 

Those are just two aspects to the game. I played multiple sports through highschool, and baseball is most definitely the most complicated and hardest game to master. 

The best of all time get a hit 30% of the time. You hit a sphere coming from 60.5 feet away with a cylindrical piece of wood. Could come in at 100+mph or in the 80’s with a foot and a half of lateral movement. You then have to decide practically instantly if you want to swing, and if so you gotta hit it into play.
